text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government is considering revising its citizenship laws to benefit overseas Vietnamese.

-- Japan might have to reduce future Official Development Assistance (ODA) loans by ten percent but adjustments would be made to ensure Vietnam is not affected, visiting Japanese parliamentarian Yoshimi Watanabe told Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai.
-- The government has decided to prepare an ordinance on operations of a stock market in addition to a law on this area.

-- 734 officials at branches of the State Bank of Vietnam and state-owned commercial banks have been disciplined. 138 of them have been prosecuted as a result of a campaign to improve the banking system which began in 1994.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has told visiting Israeli Deputy Prime Minister Rafael Eitan that Vietnam will put all efforts into realising an agreement on agricultural cooperation which has just been signed between the two countries.
-- Vietnam will auction one-year treasury notes worth 150 billion dong ($12.83 million) on Wednesday.

-- Chairman of the National Assembly Nong Duc Manh has approved Indonesian proposals to accept Laos into the Asian Inter-Parlamentary Organisation (AIPO) and give Myanmar AIPO observer status from September.
-- Water levels on the Mekong River are now 50-60 cm higher than normal, threatening the summer-autumn rice crop in the Mekong Delta.
